description:
Antariksh Syndicate is a solo deep-tech build focused on autonomous planetary systems, lunar ephemeris modeling, and geospatial computing.

Focus: Developing an operational feasibility engine for Artemis South Pole landing sites under the Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge—evaluating solar illumination profiles and Direct-to-Earth (DTE) line-of-sight communication windows against high-relief polar topography.
summary:
LunaPath is a browser-based planning aid for comparing lunar south-pole landing sites. Choose two sites and a mission date to see the Sun and Earth plotted against each site’s terrain skyline. The app estimates how many hours each site has sunlight, line of sight to Earth, and both at once over a 30-day window. It currently supports Shackleton Rim, Malapert Massif, Statio Shiv Shakti, and Nobile Rim 1.

LunaPath uses NASA LRO LOLA elevation data to build terrain horizons and NASA JPL Horizons geometry to calculate the Sun’s and Earth’s positions. Its comparison gives separate screening cues for sunlight and simultaneous Sun/Earth visibility instead of combining different mission priorities into an unexplained score. These geometric estimates can help teams compare candidate windows early; they are not power, thermal, hazard, or communications link-budget analyses.
details:
LunaPath is a static browser application built with HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Users select two supported lunar south-pole sites, set a date and UTC time, and compare local skyline views and 30-day visibility estimates. The app calculates Sun-above-terrain time, Earth line-of-sight time, and simultaneous visibility from cached NASA JPL Horizons subpoint geometry and terrain horizons generated from NASA LRO LOLA elevation products. A site comparison provides separate cues for sunlight and simultaneous visibility, without assigning invented weights to those criteria.

The project is a first-pass screening aid. It does not calculate solar power, battery performance, thermal survival, surface hazards, or radio link margin. Results are geometric estimates based on the available elevation data and two-hour samples; the app reports when requested dates fall outside its cached geometry coverage.

Tools include HTML, CSS, JavaScript, Python, NumPy, Rasterio/GDAL, and PyProj. AI assistance: OpenAI ChatGPT and Codex helped with planning, code troubleshooting/review, and drafts of project and presentation text. The NASA terrain and geometry values were obtained from NASA sources and were not AI-generated.
